prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the counter and display about 0.3–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer, with the person beyond them at roughly 1–2 m; their exact separation is uncertain because monocular depth has no calibrated metre scale. Across frames 1–3, the downward-facing counter remains the nearest large surface while the person is partly cropped above it; in frame 4 the person is centered, facing approximately toward the wearer, and appears closer and more fully visible. In frame 5, a raised hand enters extremely near the camera on the right, likely within 0.1–0.3 m and therefore within the wearer’s reach, occluding the farther person and background. The map makes near–far ordering and the hand’s strong approach clearer than RGB alone, but boundaries around the person, counter, and dark background are coarse, and the apparent distances may be distorted by reflective surfaces and frame-to-frame scale changes.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates the person from the counter-area objects: a book-like rectangular object lies low and in front of the wearer in frames 1 and 5, and a small remote-like object appears near the lower center in frame 3. The person is mostly above and behind these objects, roughly 1–2 m from the camera, while the counter objects appear within about 0.4–0.8 m; the map provides object identity and overlap ordering that are less distinct in RGB. The person remains partly outside the upper frame in frames 1–3, becomes a larger centered torso in frame 4, and frame 5 contains two disconnected person masks, including a right-side region corresponding to the very close raised arm or hand. The masks do not reliably encode facing direction or metric distance, and several body parts are merged, clipped, inconsistently colored, or omitted, making the apparent person count and separation in frame 5 uncertain.
descriptions.pose: The pose map localizes hands and major body joints: a magenta hand is low-left/center in frames 1–3, while yellow arm or upper-body joints appear above it in frames 2–4, showing the hand below and in front of the person’s upper body. In frame 4 the shoulders span the center and the arms descend on both sides, with face points near or above the top boundary; this supports a roughly frontal orientation toward the camera wearer, although gaze direction is not resolved. In frame 5 a large articulated hand skeleton occupies the center-right and is likely only 0.1–0.3 m from the lens, within the wearer’s reach, while the rest of its body is cropped or occluded. Pose reveals joint geometry and the hand’s movement toward the camera more clearly than RGB, but the tangled hand landmarks in frames 1–3, missing torso and face connections, edge clipping, and abrupt joint changes make exact limb depth, body orientation, and person-to-person spacing unreliable.
